title: Burnt Ends Chili for the Crew
displayTitle: Burnt Ends Chili for the Crew
seoTitle: Burnt Ends Chili for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Smoky brisket ends folded into hearty bean chili
subtitle: Smoky brisket ends folded into hearty bean chili
description: Chopped burnt ends enrich a tomato-bean chili that simmers in a Dutch oven on the smoker.

steps.title: Heat smoker
steps.instruction: Preheat smoker to 275°F and make sure its water pan and fuel are ready for a long cook.

steps.title: Dice burnt ends
steps.instruction: Cut burnt ends into spoon-size pieces, trimming only hard fat that will not melt.

steps.title: Sauté aromatics
steps.instruction: Sauté onion and peppers in a Dutch oven until softened, scraping up any browned bits.

steps.title: Bloom spices
steps.instruction: Stir chili powder and cumin for 30 seconds so the spices smell fragrant but do not burn.

steps.title: Build chili
steps.instruction: Add tomatoes, beans, broth, and burnt ends, stirring until the pot is evenly mixed.

steps.title: Smoke uncovered
steps.instruction: Place the Dutch oven in the smoker uncovered for 45 minutes to pick up smoke.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.instruction: Cover and smoke another hour, stirring once so the bottom does not catch.

steps.title: Check heat
steps.instruction: Bring the chili to 165°F, especially if the burnt ends were refrigerated.

steps.title: Hold chili
steps.instruction: Keep the covered pot above 140°F; add hot broth if it thickens too much.

steps.title: Ladle bowls
steps.instruction: Serve thick chili with cheese, onions, and cornbread rather than thinning it at the table.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Burnt ends — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Burnt ends and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use any smoked brisket if burnt ends are unavailable.
Smoke can become bitter if the pot stays uncovered too long.
tonightSpread: Condiments: cheddar, green onions, hot sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Burnt ends in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It turns barbecue leftovers into a complete meal and improves while held hot.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: chop burnt ends and chili vegetables 1 day ahead. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: bring chili to 165°F.
substitutions: Use smoked chuck roast for burnt ends.
Use black beans for kidney beans.
